MW4 DMZ Operation Fallen Ember Walkthrough
MW4 DMZ Operation Fallen Ember Walkthrough
Full MW4 DMZ Operation Fallen Ember walkthrough: hazmat suits, the fuel rod puzzle, decontamination, Colossus at the warhead, the boat escape and rewards.

Operation Fallen Ember is the last MW4 DMZ story mission. It sends you into the Haneul Nuclear Reactor to pull uranium fuel rods out of the reactor, clean them, secure a warhead and escape by boat while enemy helicopters chase you. It looks frightening from the lobby, but with the right gear it is one of the easier story missions, with a fun puzzle in the middle. This walkthrough covers every step, the fuel rod puzzle and the fights at the end. We finished it as a squad in the first days of DMZ.
Fallen Ember takes place at the Haneul Nuclear Reactor, an Extreme threat mission full of radiation.
Wear a hazmat suit. You find them on walls in the area and on dead bodies.
The heart of the mission is a puzzle where you match the grid code on the console to a fuel rod in the reactor pool, three times.
Clean the three rods in the decontamination chamber, then secure the warhead. Two bosses spawn there, a smoke enemy and then Colossus, who drops the boathouse key.
Escape by boat with a teammate on the boat’s machine gun to fight off the helicopters.
Rewards: a Reactor key, a Cargo Plane and cash. The mission promises $25,000 before you deploy, but the extraction summary paid us a $5,000 Story Mission Payout, so check your Bank before and after.
Operation Fallen Ember at a Glance
Before You Start: Get a Hazmat Suit
Operation Fallen Ember at a Glance
Extreme (the reactor itself shows High on the HUD)
3-Plate Armor Vest, Medkit, Gas Mask, Radiation Blockers
Breach the Reactor, Secure the Rods, Extract Decontaminated Rods
Reactor key, Cargo Plane, $25,000 promised ($5,000 paid out for us)

The enemy is moving uranium rods, and your job is to break into the reactor and take the rods before they can use them. Ghost and Lieutenant Ko support you on the ground. Fallen Ember is the last mission on the story mission tree. It sits above
, and you have to finish both of those before it opens.
Fallen Ember on the mission select screen.
Before You Start: Get a Hazmat Suit

The whole mission takes place in heavy radiation, so a hazmat suit is what makes it doable. You find them hanging on walls around the reactor and on dead bodies you search. Try to get one for every player in the squad before you start on the objectives. Bring the recommended gas mask and radiation blockers as a backup. The
makes a Gas Mask from DMZ level 26, and Radiation Blockers once you find their recipe in a match.
A hazmat suit on a wall hook at the reactor.
Head through the tunnel in front of your spawn and follow the road to the reactor gate.
The road to the reactor gate.
Work your way into the reactor building and find the control panel. Press the red button on it to lift the safety lockdown and unlock Reactor 01.
Press the red button to unlock Reactor 01.

This is the puzzle. The console in the Reactor 01 control room shows a letter and a number on a grid, for example B6. That code matches one of the fuel rods in the water of the reactor pool below. Go down to the pool, find the rod with that code and interact with it twice, once to open its container and once more to finish. Then head back up and confirm at the console.
The console then gives you the next code. Repeat the same steps for the second and third rod, three in total.
The console grid tells you which rod to pull.
Open the matching fuel rod container in the pool.
The lettered and numbered rod grid seen from above.

Take the three rods to the decontamination chamber in Reactor 02 and clean them one after another. Each one comes out as a clean depleted uranium rod. Enemies spawn in while you work, so keep someone on watch.

Follow the marker out of the reactor building to the warhead. The moment you arrive, enemy reinforcements spawn in, and the mission turns into a boss fight. Get your armor plates topped up and your squad in cover before you walk up to the marker.
Two heavy enemies come at you, one after the other.
First comes a tanky enemy who fills the area with smoke. He soaks up a lot of damage, and the smoke hides him.

Next is Colossus, the Commander with the minigun. He fires in bursts, a few seconds of shooting and then a few seconds of nothing. Stay in cover while he fires and only shoot back during the pause, or that minigun lights you up.
When Colossus goes down he drops the boathouse key. Pick it up, unlock the garage door at the boathouse and raise it.
The reinforcements come in under a cloud of smoke.

Take the boat out of the boathouse and head for the chopper. Enemies fire RPGs at you from the shore and helicopters follow the boat. Put one teammate on the boat’s machine gun to shoot the helicopters down while another drives.

Once you reach it, the chopper takes the warhead and your objective becomes escorting it until it is safe. Around that moment a nuke goes off in the distance and a DDOS knocks out your boat, so do not panic when the engine dies. The mission completes a few seconds later. Then make your way to exfil.
The nuke goes off as the mission ends.
Do not let the lobby fool you. Fallen Ember is rated Extreme and reads like a scary mission, but it is quite easy once everyone wears a hazmat suit. Without one, the radiation is what ends your run.
The real fights are the two bosses at the warhead, covered in step 6. On the boat, the helicopter missiles never hit us, so keep moving and keep the gunner firing.
, a Cargo Plane and cash. The mission promises $25,000 before you deploy, but the extraction summary paid us a $5,000 Story Mission Payout, so check your Bank before and after.

The Cargo Plane is the standout, because it lets you parachute in on an exact spot of your choosing, an infil that otherwise costs 100,000 DMZ Cash. Finishing the mission is worth 12,500 XP toward the
, and the loot around the reactor is good too.
For the rest of the story, see our walkthroughs for
shows where the Haneul Nuclear Reactor sits. For steady cash between runs, our
covers what each op paid us.
Where does Operation Fallen Ember take place?
At the Haneul Nuclear Reactor. You work through Reactor 01 and Reactor 02, then leave by boat along the coast. The area is full of radiation, so everyone in the squad should wear a hazmat suit.
How do you start Operation Fallen Ember?

Finish Operation Iron Citadel and Operation Grid Assault first. Fallen Ember sits above those two on the story mission tree and opens once both are done. Then pick it under Story Missions in Select Deployment.
How does the fuel rod puzzle work in Fallen Ember?

The console in the Reactor 01 control room shows a grid code, such as B6. That code matches one of the rods in the reactor pool below. Go down, interact with that rod twice, then confirm at the console. Do this for three rods.
It looks scary from the lobby, but it plays quite easy once your whole squad wears hazmat suits. The tough moments are the reinforcement waves at the warhead, including Colossus with his minigun.
What are the Operation Fallen Ember rewards?

Fallen Ember rewards a Reactor key, a Cargo Plane and cash. The mission promises $25,000 before you deploy, but the extraction summary paid us a $5,000 Story Mission Payout, so check your Bank before and after. The Cargo Plane lets you parachute in on an exact spot of your choosing, an infil that otherwise costs 100,000 DMZ Cash. Finishing the mission also paid 12,500 XP.

MW4 DMZ Operation Grid Assault Walkthrough
MW4 DMZ Operation Grid Assault Walkthrough
Full MW4 DMZ Operation Grid Assault walkthrough: hacking DBN Headquarters, the code segments, defending the antenna, the radio tower climb and rewards.

Operation Grid Assault is one of the harder MW4 DMZ story missions. You hack the drone control network in DBN Headquarters, collect a second code segment at Hotel Lucera, compile and upload the code while you defend an antenna, and finish by climbing a radio tower to broadcast the kill code. This walkthrough covers every step, the fights that end most runs and what the Helicopter reward actually gives you. We finished it with a full squad in the first days of DMZ.
Grid Assault unlocks after Critical Extraction, Silent Ledger and Shopping Hacks.
It takes place in The Grid, a Critical threat area, and DBN Headquarters is rated Extreme inside.
Five steps: hack the drone control, get the second code segment, compile the code, upload it while you defend the antenna, then broadcast the kill code from the radio tower.
The enemies hit hard. Peek corners, do not rush rooms and take them one at a time.
Bring a parachute for the long trips between buildings.

Rewards: Roze’s Highrise Armory key, a Helicopter infil and cash. The mission promises $25,000 before you deploy. On the other story missions we extracted from, we were paid a $5,000 Story Mission Payout instead, so check your Bank before and after.
Operation Grid Assault at a Glance
How to Start Operation Grid Assault
Operation Grid Assault at a Glance
Access the Network, Download Network Intel, Upload Kill Switch
Roze’s Highrise Armory key x1, Helicopter, $25,000 promised
The radio tower above the financial district sends out the enemy’s drone commands. Hack the network and you shut the drones down and get into the enemy’s network, with Ghost on overwatch.
Grid Assault on the Select a Mission screen.
How to Start Operation Grid Assault
Open Select Deployment, choose Story Missions and pick Operation Grid Assault. It sits one row up on the mission tree and stays locked until you finish the three earlier story missions,
. You spawn in the middle of the map and make your own way to The Grid.
Head into DBN Headquarters, an Extreme threat area once you are inside. Take the elevator up and find the drone control laptop in a server room. Hold to hack it.
Hold to hack the drone control laptop.
The hack gives you the first part of the code. The second segment is in Hotel Lucera, a building over in The Grid. A nearby SAM site controls the airspace here, so do not count on flying in.
Hotel Lucera holds the second code segment.
A SAM site controls the airspace here.
Go back to DBN Headquarters and your laptop. Hold to hack again to compile the code from both segments.
Now upload the code at the antenna and protect it until the upload finishes. Enemies push in from several sides while it runs, so hold the room and keep them off the antenna.
Protect the antenna while the code uploads.
Upload done. Now send the broadcast.
Once the upload is done, the signal is still not strong enough to send from there, so the game sends you to the radio tower that overlooks the city.
Climb the radio tower to the very top. It takes some parkour, so send your best climber while the rest of the squad covers the base. Upload the code at the top and the mission is complete.
The radio tower for the kill code broadcast.
Uploading the code at the top of the tower.

The enemies are very strong. If you stop paying attention, you are downed in an instant. Peek corners carefully, do not push into rooms, and take enemies down one at a time. That goes double for the antenna defense, where they come at you from several sides.

The other time sink is moving between buildings. DBN Headquarters and Hotel Lucera are not next to each other, and taking the stairs down every time is slow. If you have a parachute, bring it. We took the fast route instead and jumped from the top of the building to the ground, then used a Self-Revive Kit or had a teammate revive us.

, a Helicopter and cash. The key is Legendary and opens the Highrise Armory in the Netshin Tech Complex, so it sends you back into The Grid. The mission promises $25,000 before you deploy. On the other story missions we extracted from, we were paid a $5,000 Story Mission Payout instead, so check your Bank before and after.

The Helicopter is the reward that matters. It lets you spawn in with a helicopter, an infil that otherwise costs 50,000 DMZ Cash, and you keep it once you are on the map. It is very fast and speeds up the start of a match, but it has little health. One missile and it is over.
Wear the recommended 3-Plate Armor Vest and bring a Medkit.
Pack a Parachute, or a Self-Revive Kit if you plan to jump off the roof. The
makes a Disposable Parachute from DMZ level 55.
Decide before the mission who climbs the radio tower and who covers.
Play slow inside DBN Headquarters. Corners and doorways are where squads get wiped.
The Grid is one of the Critical areas on the map. Our
shows where it sits. The other hard story mission we have covered is

lists every order page. If you need to refill your Bank before the next story mission,
promise $10,000 to $20,000 per completed op, although a single op paid us $6,800 to $14,880.
How do you unlock Operation Grid Assault in MW4 DMZ?
Finish the three earlier story missions first: Operation Critical Extraction, Operation Silent Ledger and Operation Shopping Hacks. Until then it stays locked on the mission tree.
Where does Operation Grid Assault take place?

In The Grid, the walled-off financial district of Hajin City. Most of the mission happens in and around DBN Headquarters, with a detour to Hotel Lucera for the second code segment. It is a Critical threat mission, and DBN Headquarters is rated Extreme inside.
How do you broadcast the kill code in Grid Assault?

After the upload at the antenna finishes, you still have to send the broadcast. Climb the radio tower to the top and upload the code there. The climb takes some parkour, so let your best climber take it while the others cover.
What are the Operation Grid Assault rewards?

Grid Assault rewards Roze's Highrise Armory key, a Helicopter and cash. The key is Legendary and opens the Highrise Armory in the Netshin Tech Complex, inside The Grid. The mission promises $25,000 before you deploy. On the other story missions we extracted from, we were paid a $5,000 Story Mission Payout instead, so check your Bank before and after. The Helicopter reward lets you spawn in with a helicopter, an infil that otherwise costs 50,000 DMZ Cash. It is very fast but has little health, so one missile takes it down.

MW4 DMZ Operation Iron Citadel Walkthrough
MW4 DMZ Operation Iron Citadel Walkthrough
Full MW4 DMZ Operation Iron Citadel walkthrough: the access card, the random armory keycode, the strike aircraft, the SAM site, Colossus and the rewards.

Operation Iron Citadel is the hardest MW4 DMZ story mission we have played. It sends you into Chang-san Air Base, the base run by Lieutenant Bale, to find an access card, break into the armory in the bunker, steal the ordnance manifest, blow up three strike aircraft and capture a SAM site out in the open. This walkthrough covers every step, the random keycode, the fights that end most runs and what the mission pays. We played it solo first and then finished it with a full squad.
Iron Citadel takes place at Chang-san Air Base, a Critical threat mission. The base starts at Critical and turns Extreme from Admin Complex No. 2 onward, bunker included.
The walkthrough below has ten steps, from finding an access card to the exfil with the armory manifest.
The six-digit armory keycode is random every match. Read all three notes in the bunker.
Colossus, the minigun Commander, can show up in the bunker. Shoot him only between his bursts.
The SAM site at the end is the hardest part, with open ground, a swarm of enemies and other squads.

Rewards: a Bunker Access card, an LTV and cash, plus 12,500 XP. The mission promises $25,000 before you deploy. On the other story missions we extracted from, we were paid a $5,000 Story Mission Payout instead, so check your Bank before and after.
Operation Iron Citadel at a Glance
How to Start Operation Iron Citadel
Operation Iron Citadel at a Glance
Infiltrate the Base, Recon Armory Ordnance, Disrupt the Operation
Bunker Access card x1 (full name cut off in-game), LTV, $25,000 promised
The base belongs to Lieutenant Bale, and your main job is to recover his ordnance manifest. Lieutenant Ko stays on comms with you throughout the mission.
Iron Citadel on the Select a Mission screen.
How to Start Operation Iron Citadel
Open Select Deployment, choose Story Missions and pick Operation Iron Citadel. It sits one row up on the mission tree, above the three missions that close a
chapter, and stays locked until you have finished those three. Once it opens, you deploy in the North Korean Wilderness, a few hundred meters from the base.
Head for Chang-san Air Base. On the way in we ran into the Commander Colossus in the North Korean Wilderness, so stay alert before you even reach the fence.

Four search zones show up on the tac map across the base. Loot the containers inside them. Every container you open scans for the card, so keep searching zone by zone until the game tells you the keycard has been found.

The card is an Epic key called the Air Base Access Card. Ours lay on an office desk. Make sure you have backpack space, because a full backpack blocks the pickup. The mission reward at the end is the Supreme Leader’s Bunker Access Card; that card, the Air Base DRC Weapons Locker inside this armory and every other key on Hajin are in our
The four access card search zones on the base.
The Air Base Access Card on an office desk.
Take the card to Admin Complex No. 2. The keycard door there needs the Air Base Access Card. Inside, use the terminal to upgrade it and take the single-use Armory Card it gives you.

The upgrade sets off the base alarm, every soldier on the base goes on high alert, and the base turns Extreme. The armory is in the Chang-san Air Base Bunker, which you enter through the Entrance Garage. Expect heavy resistance from here on, and possibly Colossus in the bunker.
The upgrade terminal in Admin Complex No. 2.
The base alarm goes off after the upgrade.

The armory door needs a six-digit code. Three notes in the bunker each hold two of the digits. In our first run they were in the medical wing, the administration area and the Control Room. The code is random every match. Our first run used 294324, and our second run showed different digits altogether.
One of the three keycode notes.
Entering the code at the armory keypad.
Inside, find the Armory Manifest. It shows that the explosives are meant for a set of specially equipped jets parked in the hangar and out on the tarmac. Those jets are your next target.
8. Plant Explosives on the Strike Aircraft
Three jets are marked on the base. Plant explosives on all three. They are spread out, so move as a squad and clear each one before you plant.
The Armory Manifest points you to the jets.

After the jets, a SAM site on the base becomes your target. Stand at the launcher until the capture bar fills. In our first run this was the mission objective. In our second run it showed up as a side op worth 150 XP, while the mission had already moved on to the exfil, so grab it only if your squad can hold the open ground.
The last objective is to get out with the manifest. In our full run our operator went down right at the end and went Missing in Action, but the mission still counted as completed and paid 12,500 XP.
Last step: exfil the Armory Manifest.

Iron Citadel can be a very hard mission, depending on your loadout and your teammates. Our first attempt was solo and it went badly. We survived until the SAM site, and that part is the hardest. You are out in the open, the base is swarming with enemies, and other squads on the map can join the fight too.

The other big threat is Colossus, the minigun-carrying Commander that plays like a Juggernaut. We met him twice, on the way in and again in the bunker. If he shows up after you open the armory, take him out right away so you do not have to worry about him for the rest of the mission. He fires in bursts, a few seconds of shooting and then a few seconds of nothing. Only attack him when he stops, or that minigun will light you up. Colossus is also one of the three Commanders on the
Colossus showed up in the bunker garage.

Iron Citadel rewards a Bunker Access card, an LTV and cash. We have never seen the card’s full name written out in-game, so Bunker Access card is our reading of it. The mission promises $25,000 before you deploy. On the other story missions we extracted from, we were paid a $5,000 Story Mission Payout instead, so check your Bank before and after.

The LTV is the best reward. It lets you spawn in with the heavily armored LTV, an infil that otherwise costs 25,000 DMZ Cash every time you buy it. Finishing the mission is also worth 12,500 XP toward the
Bring a strong weapon. This is not a mission for a starter gun.
Wear a 2-Plate or 3-Plate Armor Vest, with 3 plates recommended.
Pack plenty of Armor Boxes and Ammo Boxes, plus a Medkit and a Self-Revive Kit if you have one. The
makes Ammo Boxes from DMZ level 12 and Armor Boxes from level 14.
Do not rush it. Build up a good operator first, with solid gear, a strong weapon and a good set of traits, then go in with two good teammates.
are a good way to build up that cash and gear first.

How do you start Operation Iron Citadel in MW4 DMZ?

Open Select Deployment, choose Story Missions and pick Operation Iron Citadel at Chang-san Air Base. It unlocks once you have finished Operation Critical Extraction, Operation Silent Ledger and Operation Shopping Hacks. It is a Critical threat mission, and the game recommends a 3-Plate Armor Vest, a Medkit and an Ammo Box.
What is the armory keycode in Operation Iron Citadel?

It changes every match. The six-digit code is split over three notes in the Chang-san Air Base Bunker, two digits per note. Our first run used 294324, and our second run showed completely different digits, so read the notes every time.
What are the Operation Iron Citadel rewards?

Iron Citadel rewards a Bunker Access card (we have never seen its full name in-game), an LTV and cash. The mission promises $25,000 before you deploy. On the other story missions we extracted from, we were paid a $5,000 Story Mission Payout instead, so check your Bank before and after. The LTV reward lets you spawn in with the armored LTV, an infil that normally costs 25,000 DMZ Cash. Finishing the mission also paid us 12,500 XP, even though our run ended Missing in Action.
Where is the SAM site in Operation Iron Citadel?

On the Chang-san Air Base itself. After you plant explosives on the three strike aircraft, a SAM site on the base becomes your target, out in the open while the base is swarming with enemies. In our first run capturing it was the mission objective. In our second run it showed up as a side op worth 150 XP, while the mission had already moved on to the exfil.
Can you do Operation Iron Citadel solo?

You can try, but it is the hardest story mission we have played. Our solo attempt made it to the SAM site before going down. With two good teammates, strong gear and plenty of armor and ammo boxes it is very doable.

MW4 DMZ Operation Shopping Hacks Walkthrough
MW4 DMZ Operation Shopping Hacks Walkthrough
MW4 DMZ Operation Shopping Hacks walkthrough for NuriGO Mall in 2026. Every step, how to get working K9 Battery Cores for the lab door, and the rewards.

Operation Shopping Hacks is the chapter-ending Story Mission of Ch. Underground in MW4 DMZ, played at NuriGO Mall in Hajin. You hack a laptop at Lieutenant Jang-ui’s encampment, use the code it gives you to open mall security, power the lab door with four K9 Battery Cores, breach five lab computers, loot the lab’s vault and leave from the rooftop exfil. We ran it on October 20, 2026, the first day of DMZ early access, and it took us about 17 minutes.
Most of that is straightforward. The lab door is not. Only a core you grab from a K9 robot dog before it explodes will power the door, and that one detail is where most squads get stuck.
Where: NuriGO Mall, threat Medium, chapter-ending mission of Ch. Underground.
Gear: 2-Plate Armor Vest, Medkit and Night Vision Goggles recommended. NVGs are optional, we did it without.
Code: the encampment laptop gives you a code for mall security. It changes every match (we got 3129 and 7813).
Lab door: needs 4 K9 Battery Cores. Loot the core from a K9 before it explodes, or you only get a useless Destroyed K9 Battery Core.
Lab computers: when one drops out with an error screen, restart the hack. The breach timer only moves with the computers running.

, Night Vision Goggles and cash. The mission promises $25,000 before you deploy. On the other story missions we extracted from, we were paid a $5,000 Story Mission Payout instead, so check your Bank before and after.

Operation Shopping Hacks at a Glance
The briefing sends you after Lieutenant Jang-ui’s encampment in the shopping district, which Overlord suspects is tied to the enemy’s weapons program. Your job is to find out what that weaponry is.
Medium (parts of the mall show High on the HUD)
2-Plate Armor Vest, Medkit, Night Vision Goggles
Hack the Network, Reprogram the Protocol, Secure any Evidence
Coin Mining Den key x1, Night Vision Goggles, $25,000 promised
About 17 minutes of radiation countdown, Rating A
The Operation Shopping Hacks briefing, objectives and rewards.
This is the longest of the three chapter-ending Story Missions. Our radiation countdown stood at 29:57 at infil and 12:45 when the mission completed, and we had taken down 50 hostiles by then.
How to Start Operation Shopping Hacks

Open Select Deployment and pick Story Missions, then choose Ch. Underground on the Choose a Chapter screen. Each Story Chapter has 2 pages and 6 DMZ Orders, and Operation Shopping Hacks is the mission that closes this chapter. Our

lists every order in it. Once you have finished it, it also joins the pool for Random Story Mission, which runs at Medium to Extreme threat and requires squad fill. Completing three random Story Missions in a week also counts toward a weekly reward. When you are not running story missions, Dynamic Ops also pay cash and XP, and our
covers every op and its rewards.
Ch. Underground ends with Operation Shopping Hacks.

(Ch. Counterfeit). Finishing all three unlocks the two harder missions,

The steps below use the exact objective names the game shows, in the order they appeared in our run.
You spawn on the tram near NuriGO Mall. Head for the marker. The encampment sits inside a building at the mall, and expect a few enemies on the way in.

The laptop is on a counter by the window inside the encampment building. Hold the interact button (F on our PC) to hack it. The objective then switches to Standby for Overlord’s Data Analysis, which only takes a few seconds.
The encampment laptop with the Hold to Hack prompt.
3. Use the Code to Unlock Mall Security

Overlord’s analysis gives you a code, and it shows up right in the objective text. Ours read Use Code 3129 to Unlock Mall Security, and in another run it was 7813. The code is random per match, so a code from a guide or video will not work for you. Read it from your own objective.

The route to mall security runs through dark storefronts. We passed a Ghost Shipment operation and the Capture SAM Site side op on the way, and luggage containers along the route are full of Chemicals and Synthetics. Near the office there is a note saying the Mall Security Office is locked for bot core v2 testing, which is your first hint at what comes next.
The code appears in the objective text. It changes every match.

The Security Annex is pitch dark. Turn on the generator first for extra light, then find the laptop on the workbench next to the robot parts and hold interact to decrypt the note. An Activate UAV Tower side op also shows up around here.
Turn on the generator before you search the annex.
5. Power the Lab Door with Robot Cores

This is the K9 Core Terminal next to the lab door, with four empty slots and an objective counter at 0/4. The note taped beside the door says the lab is locked down for testing the output of the robot dog K9 power cores. You need four working K9 Battery Cores, and the next section explains how to get them without wasting half your countdown.
The K9 Core Terminal needs four cores.
Once all four are in, the objective switches to Wait for the Lab Door to Open.

Inside the lab there are five computers to hack. After the fifth one, the lab’s network breach starts and a timer runs. Laptops drop out during the breach and need a restart while enemies push the room. More on that below.
7. Wait for the Lab Servers to Reboot, Then Loot the Lab’s Vault
When the breach finishes, the lab goes dark and you wait for the servers to reboot. Then the objective changes to Loot the Lab’s Vault, which is inside a lit tent in the lab.

Looting the vault is what moved our objective on to the exfil. The laptop on the desk in the vault room holds intel, a Project K9 internal research log marked Eyes Only, which says one sample remains in secure storage and more shipments went to other locations. We read it after the exfil objective was already up, so grab it on your way out.
The Project K9 research log in the vault room.

Head up to the roof. There you attach yourself to a balloon, a plane flies by to pick the balloons up, and the mission completes. A Chemical Storage container on the way had Nitro Compounds in our run, so check it if you pass.
Our squad did not leave together. Part of the team went to a different exfil without waiting, and the mission still completed for us. We were out on the street by City Hall when it did.
The mission completed with City Hall in view.
A Commander Deathstalker showed up at NuriGO Mall right after.
How to Get Working K9 Battery Cores for the Lab Door

This is the step that stalls most squads in Operation Shopping Hacks. The mall has machines that spawn K9 robot dogs, and the robots carry the cores. The problem is what happens when you take one down. A K9 explodes shortly after it goes down, and if you loot the core after that explosion, you get a
. That item does nothing for the lab door.
The fix is speed. Take down the K9, run straight to it and pick up the battery core before it explodes. Only then do you get a real
, a blue Rare item described as used to power robots and door circuitry. Do that four times and the terminal is full.
Looted from a K9 after it has exploded
Looted from a K9 right after you take it down, before it explodes
A Destroyed K9 Battery Core. Common, and useless for the door.
The Rare K9 Battery Core is the one you want.

That is exactly what trips people up, because the destroyed core looks like the right item until you read its name. We got our working cores from the K9s in the mall atrium, and by the time we were hacking the lab computers we still had nine working cores in the backpack, so there are plenty once you loot fast.
K9 robot dogs in the mall atrium are a good source of cores.
Check the item name before you run back to the terminal. If it says Destroyed K9 Battery Core, it will not count. Look for the blue Rare K9 Battery Core.
The 5 Lab Computers and the Error Screens

The second sticking point is the network breach. After all five lab computers are hacked, the objective turns into a breach timer with a Computers Running counter. Laptops keep dropping out with an orange error screen, and the timer stalls while they are down.

Walk up to any laptop that stopped and hold interact to restart the hack. Restarting quickly is what makes the breach go faster, because the ETA only counts down properly with the computers running. In our run it read 123 seconds with 3 of 5 running, and once we kept all five going it finished in roughly a minute and a half. Enemies and K9s keep coming during the breach, so in our run one squadmate held the room while the restarts got done.
Restart any laptop that shows the orange error screen.
Operation Shopping Hacks has its own mission rewards, and each of the two order pages of Ch. Underground pays a separate set of chapter rewards once all three of its orders are done.
Coin Mining Den key x1, Night Vision Goggles, $25,000 promised
DDOS recipe, Decoy Grenade recipe, Night Vision Goggles recipe, $20,000 cash
$20,000 cash, Basic Restock Kit, Operator Rescue Beacon, Weapon Insurance Contract

The mission promises $25,000 before you deploy. On the other story missions we extracted from, we were paid a $5,000 Story Mission Payout instead, so check your Bank before and after. The three recipes unlock new items in the 3D Printer, and our
lists what each one costs to print. Our
lists every page reward for all three chapters.

The run itself graded an A. One completed mission was worth 12,500 XP, we finished with 65 hostiles taken down and 12 loot containers opened, and it pushed us from DMZ level 7 to 9, one level short of the
The rating screen for our run, graded A.
Loadout and Squad Tips for Operation Shopping Hacks

The game warns you before deploy if you have none, but we finished the mission without them. They make the dark storefronts and the annex easier, and the generator covers the darkest room. Activision’s own
recommends NVGs for the underground mall as well. Do not skip the mission because you lack a pair, especially since the mission rewards you with one.
Bring the 2-Plate Armor Vest and Medkit the game recommends. The atrium fight for cores and the breach both throw a lot of enemies at you.
Loot the cores fast from the start. Grab every working K9 Battery Core you can, even past four, so a teammate’s mistake does not send you back to the atrium.
Agree on one exfil before you leave the vault. Our squad split up at the end, and it only worked out because the mission completed anyway.
Do not relax after the mission completes. A Commander Deathstalker spawned at NuriGO Mall right after ours, when we were down to two players and low on ammo.
Where is Operation Shopping Hacks in MW4 DMZ?

Operation Shopping Hacks takes place at NuriGO Mall on the Hajin map. It is the chapter-ending Story Mission of Ch. Underground, and you start it from the Story Missions deployment in the Select Deployment menu.
How do you get K9 Battery Cores for the lab door in Operation Shopping Hacks?

Take down a K9 robot dog and pick up its battery core right away, before the robot explodes. That gives you a K9 Battery Core, a blue Rare item. You need four of them for the K9 Core Terminal at the lab door.
Why does the Destroyed K9 Battery Core not work in MW4 DMZ?

A Destroyed K9 Battery Core is what you get when you loot the core after the K9 robot has exploded. It is a Common item and it does not power the lab door. Only the Rare K9 Battery Core counts toward the 0/4 objective.
Do you need Night Vision Goggles for Operation Shopping Hacks?

No. The game recommends them and warns you before deploy if you have none, but we finished the mission without them. They make the dark mall and Security Annex easier, and the generator in the annex gives you extra light anyway.
What is the mall security code in Operation Shopping Hacks?

The code comes from the laptop you hack at the encampment, and the objective text shows it once Overlord has analysed the data. It is random per match. We got 3129 in one run and 7813 in another, so always read it from your own objective.
What are the rewards for Operation Shopping Hacks in MW4 DMZ?

Operation Shopping Hacks rewards a Coin Mining Den key and Night Vision Goggles. The mission promises $25,000 before you deploy. On the other story missions we extracted from, we were paid a $5,000 Story Mission Payout instead, so check your Bank before and after. The mission itself gave us 12,500 XP.

MW4 DMZ Operation Silent Ledger Walkthrough
MW4 DMZ Operation Silent Ledger Walkthrough
Step-by-step MW4 DMZ Operation Silent Ledger walkthrough, from the casino generator and vault camera to the drill, the 12 cash bags and the rewards.

Operation Silent Ledger is the chapter-ending Story Mission of Ch. Counterfeit in MW4 DMZ. You enter the Heavenly Luck Casino in Cheongun Village, start a generator in the parking garage, open the vault fence through a security camera, drill the basement vault and extract the printing plates in the exfil chopper. We ran it with our squad on October 20, 2026, the first day of DMZ early access, and it took about 12 minutes from spawn to mission complete.

Honestly, it is a pretty easy mission, and a fun one. There are no elites in the casino, only a lot of regular guards, so ammo matters more than anything else. The real money is the 12 optional cash bags in the vault, and that is where most of the cash in this run comes from.
Location: Heavenly Luck Casino, Cheongun Village. Threat assessment Medium, recommended 2-Plate Armor Vest and Medkit.
Route: Approach the Casino, Start the Generator, Go to Penthouse Security, open the vault fence with a parking camera, drill the vault, loot the plates, exfil.
Cash bags: 12 in the vault at $1,500 each in our run. Put them on the truck near the vault and drive them to the exfil.
Payout: the mission promises $25,000 before you deploy, but the extraction summary paid us a $5,000 Story Mission Payout, so check your Bank before and after.
Bring plenty of ammo, an Ammo Box field upgrade and two teammates you trust. Wait for the truck before anyone exfils.

The briefing explains the story. The enemy is bankrolling its operations with stolen printing plates, and the plates sit in a marked bag inside the casino vault. You get in, recover the bag and extract.
The Operation Silent Ledger briefing, objectives and rewards.
How to Start Operation Silent Ledger

Open Select Deployment, choose Story Missions and pick Operation Silent Ledger from the list. It is the chapter-ending Story Mission of Ch. Counterfeit, a chapter with 2 pages and 6 DMZ Orders. The other two chapters end with
(Ch. Underground). Finishing all three unlocks the two harder missions,
at the Haneul Nuclear Reactor, where the story ends.

In the DMZ Orders menu, Silent Ledger is order 03 on the chapter’s second page, with the task “Complete the Operation Silent Ledger Story Mission”. Finishing the mission ticks that order off as well. Our
lists every order in the chapter.
Ch. Counterfeit has 2 pages, 6 orders and ends with Operation Silent Ledger.

The same page also has the order Eyes Everywhere, which asks you to print a Recon Drone and mark 10 enemies in the Heavenly Luck Casino with it. The casino is packed with guards during Silent Ledger, so if you already have the Recon Drone recipe from the chapter’s first page, bring a drone and stack both orders in one run. Our
lists what the drone costs to print.
These are the exact objective texts in the order the game gave them to us.

You spawn in Cheongun Village with the casino marker a few hundred meters out (291 meters on our spawn). The village is Low threat, but the casino switches to High as soon as you enter, and we had already eliminated 6 hostiles by the time we reached the front entrance.
The mission starts with a walk to the casino.

Inside, the objective changes to Start the Generator. Cross the dark casino floor past the slot machines and head down into the Heavenly Luck Casino Parking. The yellow portable generator sits in a small dark room on the parking level. If you have not been to Cheongun Village yet, our
Interacting starts a pull-start minigame. A marker sweeps across a timing bar and you press F (on PC) when it is inside the yellow sweetspot. A clean hit gives you a few XP and the generator runs.
The generator is on the parking level.
Press F when the marker is in the yellow zone.
With the power on, the objective becomes Go to Penthouse Security. Walk back through the parking lobby with the ATMs and follow the marker up to the security office.
4. Open the Vault Fence Using a Parking Level Camera

In penthouse security, find the desk with the CCTV monitor and use Security Station - Parking Levels. That opens a full-screen camera feed. On PC you switch cameras with A and D, zoom with Q and E, and there is a night vision toggle for the darker feeds. Cycle until you see the caged vault area in the basement and look at the vault fence. The fence opens and the objective jumps to Breach the Vault in the Basement.
Check the counter in the security office before you leave. We found Ballistic Flight Logs there, an Uncommon valuable worth $1,000 when you sell it at the
Use the parking level security station.
Look at the vault fence through the camera to open it.
5. Breach the Vault in the Basement

Take the elevator marked B1/B2 Parking in the casino lobby down to the basement. Place the drill on the round vault door and a Drilling Safe bar starts filling. This is the only part of the mission where you have to hold a spot, and the guards push you while it runs. Plate up before you place the drill and keep someone on each approach.
The B1/B2 Parking elevator leads to the vault.
Hold the basement while the drill runs.
6. Loot the Printing Plates from the Vault

When the drill finishes, the vault is breached and the objective changes to Loot the Printing Plates from the Vault. Grab the plates from the vault. At the same moment a side op starts that counts the cash bags you secure, 12 in total.
The cash bag side op starts as soon as the vault opens.
7. Extract the Printing Plates in the Exfil Chopper

With the plates in hand, the last objective is Extract the Printing Plates in the Exfil Chopper. The mission completes when the plates leave on a chopper. On the way out we also picked up Infantry Invasion Plans, another Uncommon $1,000 valuable, from a shelf in the parking level, and a second optional side op showed up, Repair the Vehicle (2/4 in our run).

The cash bags are optional, and skipping them is a mistake. Each bag was worth $1,500 in our run and the side op counts 12 of them. That is up to $18,000 sitting in the vault, far more than the mission’s own cash payout.

Carrying them one at a time is slow. There is a truck near the vault, so load every bag onto the back, drive it to the exfil and throw the bags into the chopper (V on PC). The cash showed up as extra money on our extraction screen.
The mission completed while we were still on the truck.
Throw the cash bags into the chopper to bank them.

Agree with your squad to wait for the truck. Our mission completed while one of us was still driving the bags, 287 meters from the rest of the squad at the exfil. The plates left, the mission counted, and the truck had to catch a later exfil at Cheongun Outskirts. Teammates who exfil before the bags arrive can miss out on a lot of cash.
Operation Silent Ledger Rewards and Payout
Operation Silent Ledger rewards a Gold Bar, a

, a Polaris Dagor A1 and cash. The Polaris Dagor A1 is an infil, just like the LTV, Helicopter and Cargo Plane from the harder story missions. It drops a light vehicle to you at the start of a match, an infil that normally costs 5,000 DMZ Cash.

The mission promises $25,000 before you deploy, but the extraction summary paid us a $5,000 Story Mission Payout, so check your Bank before and after. The same summary banked another $4,200 in cash and $9,000 in miscellaneous cash, for $18,200 in total. We also brought out 4 valuable items, 2 printer ingredients, 9 printer resources and 3 epic items.
Our extraction summary with the $5,000 Story Mission Payout.

Finishing Silent Ledger also completes order 03 on the chapter’s second page (Counterfeit 2/2). That page pays $20,000 cash, an Operator Rescue Beacon and a Weapon Insurance Contract once all three of its orders are done. The chapter’s first page (Counterfeit 1/2) pays a Recon Drone recipe, another $20,000 and an Explosives Equipment Kit, and our
Bring enough ammo and an Ammo Box field upgrade. The drill phase is where you burn through it, and our magazine was close to empty while the bar filled.
No elites, no boss. A squad that holds angles at the vault is all this mission asks for.
Wait for the marker to sit in the yellow zone before you press. If the first camera feed doesn’t show the fence, cycle cameras and use night vision.
Loot the valuables on the route.
The security office and the parking level each gave us a $1,000 valuable.

, bring it. Its description says it unlocks the small armory in the underground parking of the Heavenly Luck Casino, the same level you walk through for the generator. We found ours in a duffel at Songdo Wharf.
The Vault Armory key opens a small armory in the casino parking.
Once you finish it, Silent Ledger becomes eligible for Random Story Mission, which runs at Medium to Extreme threat with squad fill required. If you want cash and XP without a story mission, our
covers every op and its rewards. DMZ was in early access from October 20 and opened to everyone with the full launch on October 23 (
where 50,000+ members hang out, or see what our
offers for multiplayer, DMZ and Warzone.
Where is Operation Silent Ledger in MW4 DMZ?

Operation Silent Ledger takes place in the Heavenly Luck Casino in Cheongun Village on the Hajin map. It is the chapter-ending Story Mission of Ch. Counterfeit, and you pick it from the Story Missions deployment.
How do you open the vault fence in Operation Silent Ledger?

Go to Penthouse Security and use the Security Station - Parking Levels. Cycle through the parking cameras until you see the caged vault in the basement and look at the vault fence. The objective then switches to Breach the Vault in the Basement.
How do you start the generator in Operation Silent Ledger?

The generator is a yellow portable unit in the Heavenly Luck Casino Parking. Interact with it and press F (on PC) when the timing bar is inside the yellow sweetspot. A clean hit pays a little XP and the mission moves on.
Are the cash bags in Operation Silent Ledger worth taking?

Yes. The side op counts 12 cash bags in the vault and each one was worth $1,500 in our run. They are optional, so load them onto the truck near the vault and drive them to the exfil instead of carrying them one at a time.
What are the Operation Silent Ledger rewards?

Operation Silent Ledger rewards a Gold Bar, a Counting Room Vault key and a Polaris Dagor A1. The mission promises $25,000 before you deploy, but the extraction summary paid us a $5,000 Story Mission Payout, so check your Bank before and after. The Polaris Dagor A1 is an infil, a light vehicle dropped to you at the start of a match, which normally costs 5,000 DMZ Cash.
Can you replay Operation Silent Ledger in MW4 DMZ?

After your first clear, Silent Ledger joins the pool for Random Story Mission, which picks from the story missions you have already completed. A random pick can come in anywhere from Medium to Extreme threat, so it can run at a higher threat than the Medium assessment of your first clear, and it needs squad fill. Three random Story Missions in a week earn a weekly reward.

MW4 DMZ Level Rewards: Every Unlock From 2 to 70
MW4 DMZ Level Rewards: Every Unlock From 2 to 70
Every MW4 DMZ level reward from 2 to 70 with the total DMZ XP per level, when the Gunsmith, Vendor and Dog Tag Case unlock, and how to level fast.

MW4 DMZ level rewards run from DMZ level 2 to DMZ level 70, and the last level takes 1,165,573 total DMZ XP. The milestones that matter most are the 3D Printer at DMZ level 2, the Vendor at 5, the Gunsmith at 10 and the Dog Tag Case at 20, with bounty payout boosts at 30, 40, 50 and 70. We read every unlock off the in-game Progression screen on October 20, 2026, the first day of DMZ early access, and the full list sits in the filterable grid below.

We really like this system. It is a second leveling track next to your normal MW4 level, and it makes DMZ a lot more in-depth than a mode where you only chase loot. It will take you quite some time to reach a high DMZ level, though. Think of it as a nice extra grind, not something you finish in a weekend.
DMZ level is separate from your MW4 player level. Find it under Progression, DMZ Level Unlocks.
Stations: 3D Printer (DMZ level 2), Vendor (5), Gunsmith (10), Dog Tag Case (20).
Bounty payout: +10% at 30, 25% at 40, 50% at 50 and 100% at 70.
Max: DMZ level 70 at 1,165,573 total DMZ XP.
Fastest XP we saw: Story Missions (12,500 XP), Dynamic Ops (4,500 to 8,000 XP) and the Deployment Bonus.
You keep your XP when you die.

How DMZ Levels Work in MW4
Everything you do in a DMZ deployment earns
. That XP fills your DMZ level, and each DMZ level hands out rewards such as
, 3D Printer recipes, printer ingredients, Survival Kits, operator skins and permanent station upgrades. Your MW4 player level from Multiplayer is a different bar and does not unlock any of this.

To see the list in game, open Progression and pick the DMZ Level Unlocks tab. It sits next to Multiplayer Level Unlocks, Prestige and Prestige Master. The same DMZ XP also fills the bar toward your next Trait Point and raises your Dog Tag level, which climbs through ranks like Bronze and Silver.

Your DMZ level belongs to your account, not to one operator. Every Active Duty operator you play pushes the same DMZ level, and the stations and rewards it unlocks stay yours on every operator. Trait Points and the Dog Tag rank are different, because those belong to the operator who earned them. When our operator went Missing in Action, rescuing them was the way to get back that operator’s purchased Traits, unspent Trait Points and Dog Tag rank, while our DMZ level simply stayed where it was. Our
shows how we spend those Trait Points.
The Level tab after a run. DMZ level, the next unlock and the Dog Tag level all move from the same DMZ XP.

One thing confused us at first. The XP needed number on the unlocks screen is what you still need from your current XP, not the total for that DMZ level. We captured DMZ levels 2 to 30 at 0 XP and levels 31 to 70 at 42,166 XP, then added that back so every number in this post is the total. Both sets gave the same totals for levels 26 to 30, so the math checks out.

The curve is close to flat. DMZ level 2 costs 15,050 XP, and the step from 69 to 70 costs 18,634 XP. Every DMZ level asks for roughly the same effort, so the grind to 70 is long because there are 69 steps, not because the last ones are brutal.
Every DMZ Level Reward From 2 to 70

This grid holds all 90 rewards across 69 DMZ levels, each with the total DMZ XP you need. Filter it by type if you only care about recipes, stations or Survival Kits. A Recipe card unlocks that recipe on the 3D Printer for good. An Item card gives you a single copy of that item, such as a vest, a field upgrade or a fire support call-in, so you still need the recipe to print more.

MW4 DMZ Best Traits: Every Trait, Build and Prestige
The best MW4 DMZ traits for looting, PvP and team play, every Major and Minor Trait in the three trees, and how Operator Prestige works.

Traits are the perks your Operator earns in MW4 DMZ. Every Operator has three trees, Warfighter for fighting, Scout for loot and intel, and Survivalist for staying alive, and earns 18 Trait Points to spend across them. That is enough for two full trees, not three, so your choice decides what kind of Operator you play. Below are the best traits for looting, PvP and playing as a team, in three builds, followed by how the trees work, how Operator Prestige works and every trait we have found.
Our builds: Scout plus Survivalist for looting, Warfighter plus Survivalist for PvP, and Scout plus Survivalist with squad traits for team play.
Three trees per Operator: Warfighter, Scout and Survivalist. 9 rows each, one trait per row, capstones at the top.
18 Trait Points per Operator, one per Dog Tag rank. Enough for two full trees.
Rows 3, 6 and 9 hold Major Traits that are the same on every Operator. The other rows hold random Minor Traits.
Prestige resets your trees for a permanent Prestige Trait, but it is still locked in early access.

These are the builds we run on our own Operators. Each one spends all 18 Trait Points on two full trees. The Major Traits in rows 3, 6 and 9 are fixed picks. Minor Traits are random, so for the other rows each build lists the Minor Traits to take when they show up. If none of them is on offer, pick the closest match.

Major Traits in rows 3, 6 and 9 are the same on every Operator. Minor Traits are random: every Operator gets a different mix in the other rows, and a Minor Trait can even turn up in another tree. Take the ones on the list when they appear, and pick the closest match when they do not.

This is the build we level a fresh Operator with. Scout pays you more for everything you pick up: extra cash from ops and extracts, extra printer resources, a chance at an extra item in containers and radar pulses while you loot. Survivalist keeps the loot run going, with longer consumables, better crates from ops, a better chance at useful items when you run low and a free first wound repair. Numb The Pain comes last.
The Scout half of our looting build.

This build wins fights. Plate Speed, Plate Pouch and Plate Organization mean you carry more plates and put them in faster. Auto Fill and Equipment Professional keep your lethals and tacticals topped up. Combat Scanner pings a player you down, Rampage gives you a short Painkiller after a kill, Quick Fix starts your health regeneration sooner, and Possum gives you a second life once per match. Bounty Hunter pays more when you collect bounties.
Survivalist, topped by Numb The Pain.
For a squad we fill Scout and Survivalist with traits that help everyone, not just you.

Overwatch in row 9 keeps every UAV tower you activate running, so your whole squad sees enemies. UAV Upgrade in row 6 increases the range and duration of your UAVs and upgrades them to Advanced UAVs. Mini Tracker and Operator Tracker add radar pulses while you loot and enemy footprints to follow.

Faster Revive in row 3 and Numb The Pain in row 9 get teammates back up faster, with Painkiller and Smelling Salts on the revive. Impact Smokes in row 6 drops smoke when you go down, so your squad can reach you. Rescuer drags downed teammates faster, and Expedited Extraction brings the exfil in much faster for everyone.
Skip Fast Learner and Lucky here, because they only help you. Resupply is worth a point whenever it shows up, because every armor box then gives two extra plates.

Not sure where to start? Spend your first points in the tree you will use most. Two full trees beat three half-finished ones, because the capstones in row 9 only open up once the eight rows below them are filled.
How Traits Work in MW4 DMZ
Open Operators at your FOB and pick Traits. Each Operator has three trees side by side, Warfighter in red, Scout in yellow and Survivalist in teal, plus a fourth tab for Prestige.
Row 1 is a single starting trait. Rows 3, 6 and 9 have two big Major Traits, and the other rows have three Minor Traits. Row 9 holds the two capstones.
You climb from the bottom up and take one trait in every row. Rows 3, 6 and 9 are always visible, but the rows with three traits stay hidden as question marks until you take a trait in the row below.
Your Operator earns a point every time their Dog Tag ranks up, from Steel I to Onyx III. A full tree costs 9 points, so you fill two trees, never three. Our
A new Operator starts at zero again, and rescuing an MIA Operator gives their traits back.
Major Traits Are Fixed, Minor Traits Are Random

Activision calls the six big traits in rows 3, 6 and 9 Major Traits, and those were the same in every tree we checked, on four different Operators. Every other row holds Minor Traits, and those are random. Our Hunter Killer starts Survivalist with Air Superiority, our Army SF Airborne with Rad Blocker and our Min-Hee with Fuel Economy. Consumable Stacker sat in row 7 on one Operator and in row 5 on another.

A Minor Trait can even turn up in another tree. Final Intel and Resupply were Warfighter traits on our Hunter Killer, but both showed up in Min-Hee’s Survivalist tree. So there is no fixed path to copy. Pick your Major Traits, and take the Minor Traits from your build whenever they appear.
Min-Hee's Survivalist tree: a different starting trait, and Final Intel from Warfighter in row 2.
Scout and Survivalist filled. The empty Warfighter tree only shows its starting trait and rows 3, 6 and 9.
Once an Operator has all 18 Trait Points, you can Prestige them. For the first Prestige, the Prestige screen asks for three things.
All 18 Trait Points on that Operator, which means Onyx III.
Rare gear on the Operator: two weapons, a plate carrier, a backpack and four printer ingredients.

Everything left on the Operator is consumed. In return the Warfighter, Scout and Survivalist trees reset so you can level them again, and the Operator gains a permanent Prestige Trait, up to three in total. According to Activision that trait is random, and from the fourth Prestige on you are offered a new one that you can swap for one of your three. Prestiging several Operators also unlocks extra rewards.
The price goes up with every Prestige. According to Activision, the second asks for Epic gear and $300,000, and the third and every one after that Legendary gear and $500,000. Our
The 12 Prestige Traits are Pro versions of the Major Traits in rows 6 and 9, four per tree.

Where to use the Black Market Weapons Locker Key If you've got a Black Market Weapons Locker Key, you can use it to open the weapons locker in the stockroom of the Hanrim Village shop. dexerto_keys.name: Counting Room Vault
dexerto_keys.notes: The Counting Room Vault key is the reward for completing Operation Silent Ledger. It has also been reported in an industrial locker at the Rice Mill and a military locker at Haksan School, but neither spawn is guaranteed. Where to use the Counting Room Vault key If you've got the Counting Room Vault key, you can use it to open the counting room vault behind the Cashier in the Heavenly Luck Casino, Cheongun Village (F4). Head in through the main front doors, turn right into the corridor with the cages, and take the door on the left before the slots area into the security room. The vault is at the far end, behind a dark wooden door with a keypad. Expect other players here. For the full breakdown, see our Counting Room Vault guide. counting vault.name: Counting Room Vault
counting vault.notes: The Counting Room Vault key is the reward for completing Operation Silent Ledger. It has also been reported in an industrial locker at the Rice Mill and a military locker at Haksan School, but neither spawn is guaranteed. Where to use the Counting Room Vault key If you've got the Counting Room Vault key, you can use it to open the counting room vault behind the Cashier in the Heavenly Luck Casino, Cheongun Village (F4). Head in through the main front doors, turn right into the corridor with the cages, and take the door on the left before the slots area into the security room. The vault is at the far end, behind a dark wooden door with a keypad. Expect other players here. For the full breakdown, see our Counting Room Vault guide. commanders.name: Colossus
commanders.grid: Roams - B3 The Citadel, F6 Cheonwang Peak Array, B5 Chang-san Air Base
commanders.drops: Military Composites, Experimental Compounds (Legendary 3D Printer ingredients)
commanders.what_it_is: A seven-foot heavily armoured soldier carrying a minigun that fires depleted uranium rounds. Yellow canister on its back.
commanders.weakness: EXPLOSIVES DO NOTHING. Its suit is immune to grenades, thermite, C4 and drill charges. Bullets only.
how_to_beat: Skip every explosive. Bring a high-capacity automatic weapon - PPSh-41 or Cronen Squall - or a Type 73 LMG with armour-piercing rounds and a 100-round box mag.
Aim for the head and upper torso. Headshot kills are worth about 1198 XP.
Keep the boss's chassis between you and it. A parked military truck in The Citadel is ideal cover.
Get height. Climb the truck bed, or take the metal stair landing at The Armory and fire down with a Signal 50.
It sprays automatic fire down alleys and through gates, and will shred your plates. Back off around the far side of cover to re-plate whenever it closes in.
Stay out of the green gas it trails, and never stand near metal when it is close - it sends a blue electric shock that travels across nearby metal.
commanders.do_not_use: grenades, thermite, C4, drill charges and every other explosive - they do nothing to it
commanders.best_against: PPSh-41, Cronen Squall, or a Type 73 LMG with armour-piercing rounds and a 100-round box mag. A Signal 50 sniper also works from high ground.
commanders.damage_rule: BULLETS ONLY - explosives do nothing to it

commanders.name: Deathstalker
commanders.grid: Roams - H6 NuriGO Mall, G6 DBN Headquarters, I7 Songdo Wharf
commanders.drops: Prototype RF Module (Legendary - Large Secure Backpack, Fulton Drop Marker, Vendor upgrade)
commanders.what_it_is: A helicopter-sized autonomous drone with twin machine-gun turrets. Fires machine guns and rockets.
commanders.weakness: SAM sites are the clean answer. Launchers and sustained gunfire also work.
how_to_beat: BEST METHOD - capture a SAM site. Hack and hold the launcher and it shoots the Deathstalker down with one missile.
The SAM capture takes about 30 seconds. Stay in the capture zone or enemies push you out and the bar resets.
If no SAM site is close, sustained gunfire works. From the DBN Headquarters helipad a scoped sniper puts it down in roughly 25 seconds.
An LMG from a flat rooftop with a waist-high ledge works well - mount up and fire long bursts into the hull as it circles.
Break line of sight under roofs, in doorways and under railings between passes. Do not reload or apply plates in the open.
It hovers high and makes wide circles. Track it on the tac map and bait it toward your position.
commanders.do_not_use: nothing - but do not stand in the open while it makes its passes
commanders.best_against: Capture a SAM site and let the launcher fire a missile at it. Failing that, sustained gunfire into the cockpit and hull, or an LMG from a flat rooftop.
commanders.damage_rule: NORMAL DAMAGE - bullets work fine, but a captured SAM site is the cleanest kill

commanders.name: Tank
commanders.grid: Roams - patrols Hajin roads and highways, no fixed route
commanders.what_it_is: A North Korean main battle tank on high alert. Main gun kills a vehicle in one hit; the top MG kills you on foot.
commanders.weakness: Bullets do NO damage at all. Explosives only.
how_to_beat: Explosives only - any launcher, thermite, C4 or drill charge works.
A launcher is the most reliable single hit. Its reactive armour blunts RPGs, so use thermite and drill charges as well.
Stay off open fields and roads. Buildings and tight streets block its main gun.
Hit it from behind or the side, then move immediately after every shot.
Bring Ammo Boxes - this fight burns through supplies fast.
Loot three spots once it is dead: the front, the back and the top.
commanders.do_not_use: every bullet and every rifle - bullets do NO damage at all
commanders.best_against: Any launcher, thermite, C4 or drill charge. Its reactive armour blunts RPGs so bring thermite and drill charges as well. Bring Ammo Boxes.
commanders.damage_rule: EXPLOSIVES ONLY - bullets do no damage at all

boss_strategies.detail: Lieutenants take a lot of punishment and a long, loud fight makes the AI react harder. Bring enough plates and ammo. Put a launcher in your second weapon slot - for the Deathstalker pick one with lock-on. Around the Haneul Nuclear Reactor you need radiation protection: Gas Mask, Durable Gas Mask, Radiation Blockers or a Hazmat Suit.

Every lieutenant drops a Dog Tag Case. Picking it up shows your position on EVERY player's tac-map. Only grab it when an exfil is within reach and the path is clear, then head straight out and skip loot rooms. You still get the cash and XP for the kill without the case - leave it if the lobby is closing in.

Commanders have NO intel to buy - they roam Hajin, appear on your tac-map when close, and trigger a Team Leader warning. Lieutenants are on the Boss Board: buy their intel for DMZ Cash, or climb a Lieutenant Hunt Tower to mark the nearest one for free. Some lieutenant intel unlocks only after DMZ Order chapters.

Kill AI and your star rating climbs - one star brings reinforcements, five stars sends Deathstalkers, hunt squads and riot-shield units after you. It is opt-in: disengage into the woods and it calms down. Killing with a suppressed weapon does not raise the star rating, so play quiet.

Flank from multiple angles so a commander cannot lock onto a single target. Stun grenades interrupt a Colossus's tracking. Control the surrounding area and disengage if you get overwhelmed - nearby AI and rival squads will join the fight.

The Boss Board pays $50,000 for each Commander and $10,000 for lieutenant first kills. A commander kill plus EXTRACTION gives the 3D Printer ingredients - Military Composites, Experimental Compounds, Prototype RF Module, Nano-Structured Alloy - which feed the late FOB upgrades. Extract with the ingredients or you lose them.

If you want several bosses in one raid, take the Deathstalker first while you are near a SAM site, then hunt lieutenants, and do the Tank last - it burns the most ammo. Put the Colossus on a raid where you can reach The Citadel or the air base.

entities.name: Colossus
entities.grid: Roams - B3 The Citadel, F6 Cheonwang Peak Array, B5 Chang-san Air Base
entities.drops: Military Composites, Experimental Compounds (Legendary 3D Printer ingredients)
entities.what_it_is: A seven-foot heavily armoured soldier carrying a minigun that fires depleted uranium rounds. Yellow canister on its back.
entities.weakness: EXPLOSIVES DO NOTHING. Its suit is immune to grenades, thermite, C4 and drill charges. Bullets only.
how_to_beat: Skip every explosive. Bring a high-capacity automatic weapon - PPSh-41 or Cronen Squall - or a Type 73 LMG with armour-piercing rounds and a 100-round box mag.
Aim for the head and upper torso. Headshot kills are worth about 1198 XP.
Keep the boss's chassis between you and it. A parked military truck in The Citadel is ideal cover.
Get height. Climb the truck bed, or take the metal stair landing at The Armory and fire down with a Signal 50.
It sprays automatic fire down alleys and through gates, and will shred your plates. Back off around the far side of cover to re-plate whenever it closes in.
Stay out of the green gas it trails, and never stand near metal when it is close - it sends a blue electric shock that travels across nearby metal.
entities.do_not_use: grenades, thermite, C4, drill charges and every other explosive - they do nothing to it
entities.best_against: PPSh-41, Cronen Squall, or a Type 73 LMG with armour-piercing rounds and a 100-round box mag. A Signal 50 sniper also works from high ground.
entities.damage_rule: BULLETS ONLY - explosives do nothing to it

video_notes.Nv7M_k7hL4g: Short, focused Colossus kill guide. Current MW4.

entities.name: Deathstalker
entities.grid: Roams - H6 NuriGO Mall, G6 DBN Headquarters, I7 Songdo Wharf
entities.drops: Prototype RF Module (Legendary - Large Secure Backpack, Fulton Drop Marker, Vendor upgrade)
entities.what_it_is: A helicopter-sized autonomous drone with twin machine-gun turrets. Fires machine guns and rockets.
entities.weakness: SAM sites are the clean answer. Launchers and sustained gunfire also work.
how_to_beat: BEST METHOD - capture a SAM site. Hack and hold the launcher and it shoots the Deathstalker down with one missile.
The SAM capture takes about 30 seconds. Stay in the capture zone or enemies push you out and the bar resets.
If no SAM site is close, sustained gunfire works. From the DBN Headquarters helipad a scoped sniper puts it down in roughly 25 seconds.
An LMG from a flat rooftop with a waist-high ledge works well - mount up and fire long bursts into the hull as it circles.
Break line of sight under roofs, in doorways and under railings between passes. Do not reload or apply plates in the open.
It hovers high and makes wide circles. Track it on the tac map and bait it toward your position.
entities.do_not_use: nothing - but do not stand in the open while it makes its passes
entities.best_against: Capture a SAM site and let the launcher fire a missile at it. Failing that, sustained gunfire into the cockpit and hull, or an LMG from a flat rooftop.
entities.damage_rule: NORMAL DAMAGE - bullets work fine, but a captured SAM site is the cleanest kill

video_notes.B-6DgVGoGmU: The dedicated Deathstalker guide. Current MW4.
video_notes.DHgawfZox58: Shows where Deathstalker spawns. Current MW4.

entities.name: Tank
entities.grid: Roams - patrols Hajin roads and highways, no fixed route
entities.what_it_is: A North Korean main battle tank on high alert. Main gun kills a vehicle in one hit; the top MG kills you on foot.
entities.weakness: Bullets do NO damage at all. Explosives only.
how_to_beat: Explosives only - any launcher, thermite, C4 or drill charge works.
A launcher is the most reliable single hit. Its reactive armour blunts RPGs, so use thermite and drill charges as well.
Stay off open fields and roads. Buildings and tight streets block its main gun.
Hit it from behind or the side, then move immediately after every shot.
Bring Ammo Boxes - this fight burns through supplies fast.
Loot three spots once it is dead: the front, the back and the top.
entities.do_not_use: every bullet and every rifle - bullets do NO damage at all
entities.best_against: Any launcher, thermite, C4 or drill charge. Its reactive armour blunts RPGs so bring thermite and drill charges as well. Bring Ammo Boxes.
entities.damage_rule: EXPLOSIVES ONLY - bullets do no damage at all

entities.name: Bale
entities.tip: Throws smoke grenades constantly and the room is close quarters. Clear the offices, change your corridor angles, and use thermal optics to keep sight lines. A ton of enemies guard him.

video_notes.LfZQ4-IhQww: Long solo run featuring the Bale kill. Current MW4.

entities.name: The Chemist
entities.where: Haneul Nuclear Reactor, warehouse on the east side by the reactor tanks, inside the radiation zone
entities.difficulty: Moderate, but the location is lethal
entities.drops: Dog Tag, Command Office / Secure Armory key, possible Revenant marksman blueprint
entities.tip: The fight itself is not hard - the radiation is the danger. Yellow radiation you can walk through; the RED zone destroys your gas mask and if it breaks you will not get out alive. Bring a Gas Mask plus Radiation Blockers, or a Hazmat Suit for the red zone. Clear the warehouse entrance guards, then push to the rear bay. One door in, he stands among forklifts and blue drums.

entities.name: The Doctor
entities.where: Mirae General Hospital, in the parking garage
entities.drops: Dog Tag, The Doctor's Command Office key, Doctor's Salve battle rifle blueprint
entities.tip: Easiest of the lieutenants. Clear the guards and spread out so he cannot close on the whole squad at once. His key opens the Command Office on the top floor - two weapon cases and lockers inside.

video_notes.zXT7v9sgGTM: The Doctor as part of Operation Critical Extraction. Current MW4.
video_notes.3vHRMwxIhpI: Solo attempt on The Doctor. Current MW4.

entities.name: Gorani
entities.where: Forest south of Cheonwang Peak Array, the high woods above Hanrim Village
entities.drops: Dog Tag, Incisor marksman rifle blueprint (reported)
entities.tip: Deploys around fifty decoy copies of himself. They vanish when shot - do not waste ammo. Wait for the real target to commit to a position, then kill him. He also appears to teleport and throws smoke.

video_notes.i8D5yNs_jCc: Short full guide to Gorani. Current MW4.

entities.name: Iskra
entities.tip: Easiest boss in the game. She hangs out on top of the mountain. Clear the ground floor and watch doorways and stair landings as she moves.

entities.name: Jang-ui
entities.where: Netshin Tech Complex, 15th floor, in The Grid
entities.difficulty: High - the building is the danger
entities.drops: Dog Tag, Hyeon Burst assault rifle blueprint (Epic)
entities.tip: The boss is not the problem - the building is. It is packed with exploding robot dogs and laser turrets that strip a full set of plates in one shot. Clear the corridor guards before the server hall and expect reinforcements. Keyed rooms here have included auto-turrets.

entities.name: Jin-Tae
entities.drops: Dog Tag, High Roller's Fortune ISO 9 Shade blueprint (reported)
entities.tip: Basically a normal NPC - not much to him. Retreat from the gaming floor to the rear offices and control the corridor.

video_notes.T1j2laAS3vs: Jin-Tae's location and his Private Lounge key. No standalone Jin-Tae fight video exists - see the roundup guides below for the fight.

entities.no_dedicated_note: No standalone Jin-Tae fight video exists. Coverage is a key and location guide, plus the roundup chapter (5eWnbVxeDTA 7:21, qUBam_vThT8 4:05).

entities.name: Roze
entities.where: DBN Headquarters, The Grid - very top of the building
entities.tip: Her sniper one-shots you. Treat it like a PvP encounter - move unpredictably, stay behind cover, never push her in a straight line. Use the emergency stairwell and rooftop HVAC cover.

video_notes.RYe5kDIJ2rA: Roze fight with the most views. Current MW4.

entities.name: The Scavenger
entities.where: Hajin River Heights - also reported at Cheongun Village and South Island
entities.difficulty: Low, but you cannot force the spawn
entities.drops: Dog Tag, Rare ORIS 8.6 marksman rifle
entities.tip: The only lieutenant with no fixed spawn. He appears around enemies you have already killed - kill some, then camp the area and wait. Lieutenant Hunt Towers also reveal him. Use building corners and parked vehicles for cover.

video_notes.RiEbP9kuw3U: Solo Scavenger kill in free roam. Current MW4.

entities.name: The Warden
entities.where: 14th Political Prison, in the mess hall
entities.drops: Dog Tag, Incarcerator X-58 SMG blueprint (Ultra)
entities.tip: He carries a riot shield and is surrounded by enemies, and the prison is genuinely confusing to navigate. Draw the shield's attention from one angle and attack the exposed side from another. A Flashbang forces him to drop it.
